name: Trinidad and Tobago
sources: GDP $5.07bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series TTO, 1990 = 5,068,000,000. On 1.25m people that is $4,047 a head - the richest country in this Caribbean block after the Bahamas and richer per head than any Latin American state in this roster. Real growth in 1990 was +1.51% (NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG), the first positive year since 1982: Trinidad's real GDP had fallen in seven of the eight preceding years. The arithmetic checks against the exchange rate the Factbook gives - GDP of about TT$21.5bn at the pegged 4.25 TT$/US$ is $5.06bn.
Population 1.25m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series TTO, 1990 = 1,252,208.

Inflation 11.1%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, series TTO, 1990 = 11.064426. The CIA World Factbook 1991 gives 11.4% for 1989, so the two series agree on the level. The Trinidad dollar was pegged at 4.25 to the US dollar through 1989, 1990 and January 1991, and the inflation is therefore the pass-through of the 1988 devaluation and of the austerity taxes, not a currency in free fall.

Interest rate 12.9%: World Bank FR.INR.LEND, series TTO, 1990 = 12.87. Deposit rate 5.96% (FR.INR.DPST). The loader's coupled check reads 0.025 - (0.129 - 0.111) = +0.007, which is about as close to neutral as anything in the roster gets - a currency board in all but name, holding a peg while the economy contracted.

Revenue 28% of GDP: FLAGGED AS A BRACKET. World Bank GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS has NO Trinidadian observation for any year around 1990. The bracket is built from the CIA World Factbook's budget lines - revenues $1.4bn (1988 est., 1990 edition) and $1.5bn (1991 est., 1991 edition) - against this file's $5.07bn GDP, which is 27.6% and 29.6%. 28% is entered. It is high for the region and it is right in kind: the petroleum sector supplied about 40% of government revenue even after the price collapse, which is exactly why a state whose revenue base is one commodity spent the 1980s cutting.

Military 1.2% of GDP: FLAGGED, and the widest disagreement in this file. World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS has no Trinidadian entry for 1990; the series begins in 1993 at 0.494774. The CIA World Factbook 1990 and 1991 both give '$59 million, 1.6% of GDP (1989 est.)', and 0.012 is that $59m against this file's GDP. The Factbook's own 1.6% is computed against its stale $3.75bn GDP estimate, which is why the ratio entered here is lower than the ratio it quotes. CAVEAT: the Factbook's Defence Forces entry for Trinidad lists 'Trinidad and Tobago Defence Force, Trinidad and Tobago Police Service', so the $59m plausibly includes the police, and SIPRI's later 0.49% suggests the army alone was under half of it. The figure is entered high, with the reason for doubt stated, rather than split the difference silently.

Investment: FLAGGED AS A BRACKET. World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS has no Trinidadian observation before 2000 (2000 = 16.79%). The 6.0 / 9.0 split totals 15% and is anchored only at the public end, by the CIA World Factbook 1990's capital expenditures of $430m (1988 est.) against a shrinking base. Trinidad's investment ratio had collapsed with the oil price - the Point Lisas industrial estate was built in the boom and nothing on that scale was started after 1982 - and 15% is entered as the low figure that fact implies. It is the least defensible number in this file.

Debt 49% of GDP: FLAGGED. World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS has no Trinidadian entry - Trinidad was not a Debtor Reporting System country - so this is the CIA World Factbook 1991's external debt of $2.5bn (1989) against this file's GDP, which is 49.3%. The 1990 edition gave $2.02bn at December 1987. Trinidad rescheduled with the Paris Club in January 1989 and again in April 1990 and was inside an IMF standby through the start date.

Oil 0.15 mbd: EIA international crude oil production, Trinidad and Tobago, 1990 = 150,000 barrels a day (1991 = 151,000). The USGS Minerals Yearbook for 1991 reports 56 million barrels produced in 1990, which is 153,000 a day, so the two agree. This is the whole of Trinidad's problem in one number: peak production was 240,000 b/d in 1981, the price then halved, and the country in this file is the country that fell off that. Natural gas and the ammonia and methanol plants at Point Lisas were the future and are not in this model's commodity set.

TFP trend -0.004: negative, and it is the oil. Between 1982 and 1989 real GDP fell about 30% and real GDP per head fell further; the non-oil economy was propped up by state enterprises the government could no longer fund, unemployment hit 22% in 1988, and the NAR's answer was a 10% cut in public-sector wages. Set between Cameroon's -0.008 and Ethiopia's -0.005 on the negative side and above Argentina's -0.008. It is not as negative as Peru's -0.015 because Trinidad's decline was a price shock to a functioning economy rather than an economy coming apart.

Stability 50 and authoritarianism 0.14: a Westminster democracy, a republic since 1976, with the freest press in the Caribbean and a government in January 1990 that had lost the country. The National Alliance for Reconstruction had won 33 of 36 seats in December 1986 on 66% of the vote - the largest mandate in Trinidadian history, ending thirty years of People's National Movement rule - and then broke itself on the IMF programme: Basdeo Panday and three colleagues were expelled in 1988 and founded the United National Congress in April 1989, taking the Indo-Trinidadian half of the coalition with them. Stability 50 is set level with Albania's 50, above Yugoslavia's 44, and below Cameroon's 52, and it is deliberately not lower: on 27 July 1990, seven months past the start date, 114 members of the Jamaat al Muslimeen stormed the Red House and Trinidad and Tobago Television, held the Prime Minister and most of the Cabinet hostage for six days, shot Robinson in the leg, and 24 people died. That is NOT encoded here. It is exactly the sort of thing the sim is supposed to be able to produce out of a state under fiscal stress, and writing the outcome into the start state would be scripting it.

Separatism 0.05: Tobago. The smaller island is 5% of the population, was administered separately from Trinidad until 1889, and got its own Tobago House of Assembly back in 1980 after a campaign led by A. N. R. Robinson, who was Tobago's own member of parliament and who in January 1990 was Prime Minister of the whole country. The strain is real, constitutional and entirely peaceful - a demand for internal self-government that produced the 1987 and 1996 THA acts rather than a demand to leave. Set level with Italy's 0.05 and below Senegal's 0.15. The Indo-Trinidadian / Afro-Trinidadian cleavage that decides Trinidadian elections is deliberately NOT in this number: it is a division of the electorate, not of the territory, and it belongs in the party table.

Military strength 0.8: the Trinidad and Tobago Defence Force was about 2,650 - two infantry battalions and a coast guard - with no aircraft and no armour. It is the smallest army in this roster and the number says so. What it could actually do was demonstrated in July 1990, when it retook the television station and contained the Red House in six days.

pop_growth_1990 = 1.1435%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series TTO (Trinidad and Tobago): 1,172,984 in 1984 to 1,241,600 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: TTO.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 82% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: TTO, 1990 = 82%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name. The 1989 value of the same series is 77%, on the other side of the 80% line: THRESHOLD-SENSITIVE CELL.
